figures.title: Copies occur at resize boundaries
figures.description: Starting at capacity one, appending the first item copies none. Appends two, three and five copy one, two and four old items. Append four copies none. Five appends perform five new-item assignments plus seven growth copies.

figures.title: Logical order survives physical wraparound
figures.description: For a capacity-two queue, slots zero and one contain A and B with head zero and count two. Dequeue clears slot zero and moves head to one. Enqueue C writes slot zero, leaving physical slots C and B but logical order B then C.

figures.title: A min-heap is not a binary search tree
figures.description: Array [1,2,9,5] represents a min-heap: index zero has value one and children at indexes one and two with values two and nine. Index one has a left child at index three with value five. Parent values never exceed their children, but left children need not be smaller than parents.

figures.title: Both prerequisites must complete
figures.description: A and B are prerequisites of C, and C is a prerequisite of D. In the shown snapshot A is complete and B is pending, so C and D remain blocked. Completing B can make C eligible, but D still requires C to complete.

figures.title: A shrinking interval finds the first match
figures.description: For sorted values [1,2,2,5,9] and target two, the interval starts at [0,5). Midpoint two has value two, so hi becomes two. Midpoint one has value two, so hi becomes one. Midpoint zero has value one, so lo becomes one. Equal bounds return index one.

figures.title: Optimize a stage, then recompute the whole path
figures.description: The illustrative sequential request parses for two milliseconds, fetches for forty, computes for eight and serializes for three, totaling fifty-three. Halving only computation to four milliseconds reduces the total to forty-nine. All stages are sequential with no queueing or overlap.

figures.title: Ready is different from running
figures.description: Created work becomes ready and is dispatched to running. Running work can be preempted back to ready, block while waiting for I/O or synchronization, or terminate. A waiting operation becomes ready when its wait condition is satisfied; only a scheduler dispatch makes it run.

figures.title: Reachability determines collection eligibility
figures.description: A runtime root reaches a cache, which strongly references a small view, which retains a large backing buffer. Separately, objects X and Y reference each other but have no root path. The rooted chain stays reachable; the isolated cycle is eligible for tracing collection.

figures.title: Capacity feedback constrains production
figures.description: The producer offers work to a bounded buffer. The consumer removes work from the buffer. When capacity is exhausted, feedback pauses or rejects further offers according to policy. When capacity returns, feedback can allow production to resume. This describes flow control, not durability or guaranteed completion.

figures.title: An await splits the check from the update
figures.description: Both reserve calls check remaining equal to one and suspend at the shared gate. The gate is released once. A resumes and decrements remaining to zero, returning true. B then resumes and decrements it to minus one, returning true. This is one possible continuation order and violates capacity safety.

figures.title: A circular wait has no enabled release
figures.description: Worker A holds the only instance of X and waits for Y held by B. Worker B holds the only instance of Y and waits for X held by A. Wait-for edges point from each blocked worker to the holder it needs. Neither releases while waiting, so neither can progress without recovery.

figures.title: Terminal attempts have no outgoing transitions
figures.description: Queued can start to Running or cancel to Cancelled. Running can complete to Succeeded, fail to Failed, or cancel to Cancelled. Succeeded, Failed and Cancelled have no outgoing permitted transitions. Guards and rejected outcomes are defined in the adjacent transition table.

figures.title: Caller knowledge can lag the actual outcome
figures.description: A caller submits attempt R. The service confirms R but its response is lost. The caller times out and knows only that R is unresolved to it, while the service remains confirmed. Later the caller asks for the outcome of R and learns it was confirmed. No second reservation is created by this conceptual reconciliation.
